name: Potatoes
summary: Starchy, waxy and all-purpose potatoes, which to use for what, and how to boil, mash, roast and bake them.

rows: Creamy, holds its shape fairly well
Potato salad, boiling, soups, roasting whole

items: Cut potatoes into even chunks and put them in a pot of **cold**, well-salted water. Starting cold cooks them evenly to the middle.
Bring to a boil, then simmer until a knife slides in with no resistance, about 15–20 minutes for chunks.
Drain well and let them steam dry in the pot for a minute or two.
For mash, warm the butter and milk or cream before adding, and use a masher or ricer. A blender or food processor makes them gluey.

sections.heading: Crisp roast potatoes

items: Cut into chunks and parboil in salted water for about 8 minutes, until the edges just soften.
Drain and shake them in the pot to rough up the surfaces: the fluffy edges are what crisp.
Toss with plenty of oil or fat on a preheated sheet pan and roast at 425°F (220°C) for 35–45 minutes, turning once, until deep golden.

blocks: Short on time? Skip the parboil: cut smaller, toss in oil and salt, and roast at the same temperature, turning once.

sections.heading: Baked potatoes
blocks: Scrub russets, prick them a few times, rub with oil and salt, and bake directly on the rack at 400–425°F (200–220°C) for 45–60 minutes, until a knife slides in easily. Skip the foil if you want crisp skin.

sections.heading: Storing
blocks: Keep potatoes somewhere cool, dark and dry, not in the fridge (cold turns their starch to sugar) and away from onions. Cut off green patches and sprouts before cooking: the green parts contain solanine, which is bitter and can upset your stomach in quantity.
